children.name: Macaca
children.description: The most geographically widespread primate genus after Homo, with over 20 species distributed from Gibraltar to Japan. Macaques are highly adaptable, thriving in tropical forests, snowy mountains, and urban environments alike, and are widely used in biomedical research.

children.name: Macaca mulatta
children.description: The rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta), colloquially rhesus monkey, is a species of Old World monkey in the Macaca genus.

children.name: Macaca fascicularis
children.description: Macaca fascicularis, variously known by common names such as crab-eating macaque, long-tailed macaque, or cynomolgus monkey, is a macaque species native to Southeast Asia..

children.name: Macaca fuscata
children.description: The Japanese macaque (Macaca fuscata), also known as the snow monkey, is a terrestrial Old World monkey species that is native to Japan.

children.name: Macaca sylvanus
children.description: The Barbary macaque (Macaca sylvanus) is a macaque species native to the Atlas Mountains of Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia, along with a small introduced population in Gibraltar.

children.name: Macaca nigra
children.description: The Celebes crested macaque (Macaca nigra), also known as the crested black macaque, Sulawesi crested macaque, or the black ape, is an Old World monkey that lives in the tropical regions of north Sulawesi.

children.name: Macaca nemestrina
children.description: The southern pig-tailed macaque (Macaca nemestrina), also known as the Sundaland pig-tailed macaque and the Sunda pig-tailed macaque, is a medium-sized macaque that lives in Sundaland, southern Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia..

children.name: Macaca thibetana
children.description: The Tibetan macaque (Macaca thibetana), also known as Père David's Macaque, This species lives in subtropical forests (mixed deciduous to evergreen) at elevations from above sea level.

children.name: Macaca arctoides
children.description: The stump-tailed macaque (Macaca arctoides), also called the bear macaque, is a species of macaque native to South Asia and Southeast Asia..

children.name: Macaca assamensis
children.description: The Assam macaque (Macaca assamensis) or Assamese macaque is a macaque of the Old World monkey family native to South and Southeast Asia. Since 2008, it has been listed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List, as it is experiencing significant declines due to poaching, habitat degradation, and fragmentation.

children.name: Macaca radiata
children.description: The bonnet macaque (Macaca radiata), also known as zati, is a species of macaque endemic to southern India.

children.name: Macaca sinica
children.description: }} between two toque macaques]] The toque macaque (; Macaca sinica) is a reddish-brown-coloured Old World monkey endemic to Sri Lanka, where it is known as the or rilawa (Sinhala: රිළවා), (hence the English word "rillow").

children.name: Macaca silenus
children.description: The lion-tailed macaque, locally called wanderoo, is an Old World monkey endemic to the Western Ghats of South India.

children.name: Macaca tonkeana
children.description: The Tonkean black macaque or Tonkean macaque (Macaca tonkeana) is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

children.name: Macaca maura
children.description: The Moor macaque (Macaca maura) is a macaque species with brown/black body fur with a pale rump patch and pink bare skin on the rump.

children.name: Macaca ochreata
children.description: The booted macaque (Macaca ochreata) is a macaque of the Sulawesi Island, Indonesia.

children.name: Macaca nigrescens
children.description: The Gorontalo macaque or Dumoga-bone macaque (Macaca nigrescens) is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

children.name: Macaca hecki
children.description: The Heck's macaque (Macaca hecki) is a macaque of Sulawesi, Indonesia..

children.name: Macaca leonina
children.description: The northern pig-tailed macaque (Macaca leonina) is a vulnerable species of macaque in the subfamily Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Macaca pagensis
children.description: The Pagai Island macaque (Macaca pagensis), also known as the Pagai macaque or Bokkoi, is an Old World monkey endemic to the Mentawai Islands off the west coast of Sumatra..

children.name: Macaca siberu
children.description: The Siberut macaque is a vulnerable species of macaque, which is endemic to Siberut Island in Indonesia. It was formerly considered conspecific with the Pagai Island macaque which is overall paler in color, but this arrangement was polyphyletic. Both were formerly considered subspecies of the southern pig-tailed macaque.

children.name: Macaca cyclopis
children.description: The Formosan rock macaque (Macaca cyclopis), also known as the Formosan rock monkey or Taiwanese macaque, is a macaque endemic to the island of Taiwan, which has also been introduced to Japan..

children.name: Macaca munzala
children.description: The Arunachal macaque is a macaque native to Eastern Himalayas of Bhutan, China and India. It is listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List.

children.name: Macaca brunnescens
children.description: Found on Buton Island and several small adjacent islands off southeastern Sulawesi, sometimes treated as a subspecies of M. ochreata. Its restricted range and ongoing habitat loss place it in the Vulnerable category on the IUCN Red List.

children.name: Macaca selai
children.authorship: Ghosh, Thakur, Singh, Durra, Sharma, Chandra & Banerjee, 2022

children.name: Papio
children.description: Baboons are large, terrestrial Old World monkeys native to the open woodlands and savannas of Africa and Arabia. They live in multi-male, multi-female troops of up to 200 individuals and are among the most successful primates on the continent.

children.name: Papio anubis
children.description: The olive baboon (Papio anubis), also called the Anubis baboon, is a member of the family Cercopithecidae Old World monkeys.

children.name: Papio cynocephalus
children.description: The yellow baboon (Papio cynocephalus) is a baboon in the family of Old World monkeys.

children.name: Papio ursinus
children.description: The chacma baboon (Papio ursinus), also known as the Cape baboon, is, like all other baboons, from the Old World monkey family.

children.name: Papio hamadryas
children.description: The hamadryas baboon (Papio hamadryas ; ; ) is a species of baboon within the Old World monkey family.

children.name: Papio kindae
children.description: The Kinda baboon (Papio kindae) is a species of baboon present in the miombo woodlands of Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Zambia, and possibly western Tanzania.

children.name: Papio papio
children.description: The Guinea baboon (Papio papio) is a baboon from the Old World monkey family.

children.name: Mandrillus
children.description: The mandrill is the world's largest monkey and the most colourful mammal, with males displaying vivid blue and red facial markings that intensify with dominance. Both species inhabit the rainforests of west-central Africa and live in large multi-male groups.

children.name: Mandrillus sphinx
children.description: The mandrill (Mandrillus sphinx) is a large Old World monkey native to west central Africa..

children.name: Mandrillus leucophaeus
children.description: The drill (Mandrillus leucophaeus) is a primate of the family Cercopithecidae (Old World monkeys), related to baboons and even more closely to the mandrill..

children.name: Theropithecus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the gelada, a grass-eating monkey of the Ethiopian highlands and the only surviving member of a once-diverse lineage. Geladas live in the largest primate groups of any non-human, with herds of up to 600 individuals.

children.name: Theropithecus gelada
children.description: The gelada (Theropithecus gelada, Amharic: ጭላዳ, romanized: č̣əlada, Oromo: Jaldeessa daabee), sometimes called the bleeding-heart monkey or the gelada baboon, is a species of Old World monkey found only in the Ethiopian Highlands, living at elevations of 1,800–4,400 m (5,900–14,400 ft) above sea level..

children.name: Cercocebus
children.description: Mangabeys are medium-sized, semi-terrestrial monkeys of African lowland forests, closely related to mandrills and baboons. They are specialist hard-object feeders, with robust jaws and deep molar reliefs allowing them to crack seeds and pods that other monkeys cannot exploit.

children.name: Cercocebus torquatus
children.description: The collared mangabey (Cercocebus torquatus), also called red-capped mangabey and white-collared mangabey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae of Old World monkeys.

children.name: Cercocebus atys
children.description: The sooty mangabey (Cercocebus atys) is an Old World monkey found in forests from Senegal in a margin along the coast down to the Ivory Coast.

children.name: Cercocebus agilis
children.description: The agile mangabey (Cercocebus agilis) is an Old World monkey of the white-eyelid mangabey group found in swampy forests of Central Africa in Equatorial Guinea, Cameroon, Gabon, Central African Republic, Republic of Congo, and DR Congo.

children.name: Cercocebus chrysogaster
children.description: The golden-bellied mangabey (Cercocebus chrysogaster) is an Endangered Old World monkey found in swampy, humid forests south of the Congo River in the Democratic Republic of the Congo..

children.name: Cercocebus galeritus
children.description: The Tana River mangabey (Cercocebus galeritus) is a highly endangered species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Cercocebus lunulatus
children.description: The white-naped mangabey (Cercocebus lunulatus) is a species of Old World monkey in the subfamily Cercopithecinae..

children.name: Lophocebus
children.description: Black mangabeys are arboreal Old World monkeys of central African forests, more closely related to baboons than to the semi-terrestrial Cercocebus mangabeys despite their similar appearance — a classic example of convergent evolution. They bear conspicuous crests and eyelid colouration.

children.name: Lophocebus albigena
children.description: The grey-cheeked mangabey (Lophocebus albigena), also known as the white-cheeked mangabey, is an Old World monkey found in the forests of Central Africa..

children.name: Lophocebus aterrimus
children.description: The black crested mangabey (Lophocebus aterrimus) is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Lophocebus johnstoni
children.description: Johnston's mangabey (Lophocebus albigena johnstoni) is a subspecies of the gray-cheeked mangabey (L..

children.name: Lophocebus opdenboschi
children.description: Opdenbosch's mangabey (Lophocebus aterrimus opdenboschi) is a subspecies of crested mangabey in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Rungwecebus
children.description: A monotypic genus erected in 2005 for the kipunji, the first new African monkey genus described in 83 years. Discovered independently by two field teams in Tanzania's Southern Highlands and Udzungwa Mountains, the kipunji was initially misidentified as a Lophocebus mangabey.

children.name: Rungwecebus kipunji
children.description: The kipunji (Rungwecebus kipunji), also known as the highland mangabey, is a species of Old World monkey that lives in the highland forests of Tanzania..

children.name: Cercopithecus
children.description: The guenons — a large, diverse genus of small to medium-sized forest monkeys — are the most species-rich primate genus in Africa. Each species typically has a distinctive facial pattern, which facilitates species recognition in the mixed-species groups they often form.

children.name: Cercopithecus mitis
children.description: The blue monkey or diademed monkey (Cercopithecus mitis) is a species of Old World monkey native to Central and East Africa, ranging from the upper Congo River basin east to the East African Rift and south to northern Angola and Zambia and populations further south down to South Africa.

children.name: Cercopithecus diana
children.description: The Diana monkey (Cercopithecus diana) is an Old World monkey found in the high canopy forests in Sierra Leone, Liberia, and western Côte d'Ivoire Named for its white brow which is said to resemble the bow of the Roman goddess Diana, this black-grey guenon has a white throat, crescent-shaped browband, ruff and beard.

children.name: Cercopithecus neglectus
children.description: De Brazza's monkey (Cercopithecus neglectus) is an Old World monkey endemic to the riverine and swamp forests of central Africa..

children.name: Cercopithecus nictitans
children.description: The greater spot-nosed monkey or putty-nosed monkey (Cercopithecus nictitans) is one of the smallest Old World monkeys..

children.name: Cercopithecus petaurista
children.description: The lesser spot-nosed monkey (Cercopithecus petaurista), also known as the lesser spot-nosed guenon, lesser white-nosed guenon, or lesser white-nosed monkey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Cercopithecus ascanius
children.description: The red-tailed monkey (Cercopithecus ascanius), also known as the black-cheeked white-nosed monkey, red-tailed guenon, redtail monkey, or Schmidt's guenon, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Cercopithecus mona
children.description: The mona monkey (Cercopithecus mona) is an Old World monkey that lives in western Africa between Ghana and Cameroon.

children.name: Cercopithecus campbelli
children.description: Campbell's mona monkey (Cercopithecus campbelli), also known as Campbell's guenon and Campbell's monkey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae found in the Ivory Coast, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Senegal, and Sierra Leone..

children.name: Cercopithecus lowei
children.description: Lowe's mona monkey (Cercopithecus lowei) is an Old World monkey in the family Cercopithecidae found from the Ivory Coast to Ghana..

children.name: Cercopithecus pogonias
children.description: The crested mona monkey, also known as the crowned guenon, crowned monkey, golden-bellied guenon, or golden-bellied monkey, (Cercopithecus pogonias), is a species of African primate in the family Cercopithecidae found in west central Africa..

children.name: Cercopithecus erythrogaster
children.description: The white-throated guenon (Cercopithecus erythrogaster), also known as the red-bellied monkey and the red-bellied guenon, is a diurnal primate that lives on trees of rainforests or tropical areas of Nigeria and Benin..

children.name: Cercopithecus erythrotis
children.description: The red-eared guenon (Cercopithecus erythrotis), also called red-eared monkey or russet-eared guenon, is a primate species in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Cercopithecus hamlyni
children.description: The Hamlyn's monkey (Cercopithecus hamlyni), also known as the owl-faced monkey, is a species of Old World monkey that inhabits the bamboo and primary rainforests of the Congo..

children.name: Cercopithecus wolfi
children.description: Wolf's mona monkey (Cercopithecus wolfi), also called Wolf's guenon, is a colourful Old World monkey in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Cercopithecus denti
children.description: Dent's mona monkey (Cercopithecus denti) is an Old World monkey in the family Cercopithecidae found in Central Africa..

children.name: Cercopithecus dryas
children.description: The Dryas monkey (Chlorocebus dryas), also known as Salonga monkey, ekele, or inoko, is a little-known species of Old World monkey found only in the Congo Basin, restricted to the left bank of the Congo River.

children.name: Cercopithecus roloway
children.description: The Roloway monkey (Cercopithecus roloway) is an endangered species of Old World monkey endemic to tropical West Africa.

children.name: Cercopithecus preussi
children.description: The Preuss's monkey (Allochrocebus preussi), also known as Preuss's guenon, is a diurnal primate that lives terrestrially in mountainous (up to 2500 m) forests of eastern Nigeria, western Cameroon and Bioko in Equatorial Guinea..

children.name: Cercopithecus doggetti
children.description: The silver monkey (Cercopithecus mitis doggetti) is a subspecies of the blue monkey (Cercopithecus mitis).

children.name: Cercopithecus kandti
children.description: The golden monkey (Cercopithecus mitis kandti) is a subspecies of the blue monkey.

children.name: Cercopithecus sclateri
children.description: Sclater's guenon (Cercopithecus sclateri), also known as Sclater's monkey and the Nigerian monkey, is an Old World monkey that was first described by Reginald Innes Pocock in 1904 and named after Philip Sclater..

children.name: Cercopithecus lomamiensis
children.authorship: Hart, Detwiler, Gilbert, Burrell, Fuller, Emetshu, Hart, Vosper, Sargis & Tosi, 2012

children.name: Allochrocebus
children.description: A small genus of ground-dwelling guenons of central and west-central Africa, separated from Cercopithecus based on molecular and morphological evidence. These species are more terrestrial than typical guenons and inhabit montane and submontane forests.

children.name: Allochrocebus lhoesti
children.description: L'Hoest's monkey (Allochrocebus lhoesti), also known as the mountain monkey, is a guenon found in the upper eastern Congo Basin..

children.name: Allochrocebus solatus
children.description: The sun-tailed monkey (Allochrocebus solatus) from Gabon is one of the least studied primates in its habitat..

children.name: Allochrocebus preussi
children.description: The Preuss's monkey (Allochrocebus preussi), also known as Preuss's guenon, is a diurnal primate that lives terrestrially in mountainous (up to 2500 m) forests of eastern Nigeria, western Cameroon and Bioko in Equatorial Guinea..

children.name: Erythrocebus
children.description: The patas monkey is the fastest-running primate, capable of reaching 55 km/h. A specialised open-country species of the African savanna belt, it is the most terrestrial of the guenon-like monkeys and has long limbs adapted for ground locomotion.

children.name: Erythrocebus patas
children.description: The common patas monkey (Erythrocebus patas), also known as the hussar monkey, is a ground-dwelling monkey distributed over semi-arid areas of West Africa, and into East Africa.

children.name: Miopithecus
children.description: The talapoins are the smallest Old World monkeys, with a round head, large eyes, and a bright green coat. They are highly social and semi-aquatic, living in large groups along rivers and flooded forests of equatorial Africa.

children.name: Miopithecus talapoin
children.description: The Angolan talapoin (Miopithecus talapoin), also known as the southern talapoin, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

children.name: Miopithecus ogouensis
children.description: The Gabon talapoin (Miopithecus ogouensis), also known as the northern talapoin, is a small species of African monkey native to riparian habitats in Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, the western Republic of the Congo and the far western Democratic Republic of Congo.

children.name: Allenopithecus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Allen's swamp monkey, the most plesiomorphic cercopithecine and a morphological outlier among the guenon lineage. It is placed in its own subfamily by some authorities due to its distinctive anatomy and behaviour.

children.name: Allenopithecus nigroviridis
children.description: Allen's swamp monkey (Allenopithecus nigroviridis) is a species of Old World monkey endemic to swamps and riparian forests in the central Congo Basin..

children.name: Chlorocebus
children.description: Vervet monkeys are among the most studied primates in the wild, renowned for their distinct alarm calls that discriminate between aerial and terrestrial predators. Highly adaptable, they occupy habitats from forest edge to semi-arid savanna across sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Chlorocebus pygerythrus
children.description: The vervet monkey (Chlorocebus pygerythrus), or simply vervet, is an Old World monkey of the family Cercopithecidae native to Africa.

children.name: Chlorocebus sabaeus
children.description: The green monkey (Chlorocebus sabaeus), also known as the sabaeus monkey, is an Old World monkey with golden-green fur and pale hands and feet.

children.name: Chlorocebus aethiops
children.description: The grivet (Chlorocebus aethiops) is an Old World monkey with long white tufts of hair along the sides of its face..

children.name: Chlorocebus tantalus
children.description: The tantalus monkey (Chlorocebus tantalus) is an Old World monkey from Africa that ranges from Ghana to Sudan.

children.name: Chlorocebus cynosuros
children.description: The malbrouck (Chlorocebus cynosuros) is an Old World primate from Africa that belongs to the genus Chlorocebus..

children.name: Chlorocebus djamdjamensis
children.description: The Bale Mountains vervet (Chlorocebus djamdjamensis) is a terrestrial Old World monkey endemic to Ethiopia, found in the bamboo forests of the Bale Mountains..

children.name: Colobus
children.description: Colobus monkeys are the only Old World monkeys that lack a thumb, an adaptation for rapid arboreal movement through forest canopies. They are specialist leaf-eaters with complex, multi-chambered stomachs that ferment tough foliage.

children.name: Colobus guereza
children.description: The mantled guereza (Colobus guereza), also known simply as the guereza, the eastern black-and-white colobus, or the Abyssinian black-and-white colobus, is a black-and-white colobus, a type of Old World monkey.

children.name: Colobus polykomos
children.description: The king colobus (Colobus polykomos), also known as the western black-and-white colobus, is a species of Old World monkey, found in lowland and mountain rainforests in a region stretching from Senegal, through Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia to the Ivory Coast.

children.name: Colobus angolensis
children.description: The Angola colobus (Colobus angolensis), Angolan black-and-white colobus, or Angolan colobus is a primate species of Old World monkey belonging to the genus Colobus.

children.name: Colobus satanas
children.description: The black colobus (Colobus satanas), or satanic black colobus, is a species of Old World monkey belonging to the genus Colobus.

children.name: Colobus vellerosus
children.description: The ursine colobus (Colobus vellerosus), also known as the white-thighed colobus, Geoffroy's black-and-white colobus, or the white-thighed black-and-white colobus, is a West African species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

children.name: Colobus congoensis
children.authorship: J. Hart, Amboko, Arenson, Horton, Coates, Kapale, Koko, T. Hart, Gilbert, Sargis & Detwiler, 2026

children.name: Piliocolobus
children.description: Red colobus monkeys, among the most hunted primates in Africa and a preferred prey of chimpanzees. Several species are critically endangered due to habitat loss and hunting pressure.

children.name: Piliocolobus badius
children.description: The western red colobus (Piliocolobus badius), also known as the bay red colobus, rust red colobus or Upper Guinea red colobus, is a species of Old World monkey in West African forests from Senegal to Ghana..

children.name: Piliocolobus tephrosceles
children.description: The Ugandan red colobus (Piliocolobus tephrosceles) or ashy red colobus is an endangered species of red colobus monkey, recognised as a distinct species since 2001..

children.name: Piliocolobus rufomitratus
children.description: The Tana River red colobus (Piliocolobus rufomitratus), also called the eastern red colobus, is a highly endangered species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Piliocolobus kirkii
children.description: The Zanzibar red colobus (Piliocolobus kirkii) is a species of red colobus monkey endemic to Unguja, the main island of the Zanzibar Archipelago, off the coast of Tanzania.

children.name: Piliocolobus gordonorum
children.description: The Udzungwa red colobus (Piliocolobus gordonorum), also known as the Uzungwa red colobus or Iringa red colobus, is a species of the primate family Cercopithecidae that is endemic to riverine and montane forests in the Udzungwa Mountains in Tanzania..

children.name: Piliocolobus foai
children.description: Foa's red colobus (Piliocolobus foai) or the Central African red colobus, is a species of red colobus monkey found in the Democratic Republic of the Congo..

children.name: Piliocolobus pennantii
children.description: Pennant's colobus or Pennant's red colobus (Piliocolobus pennantii) is a species of tree-dwelling primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Piliocolobus oustaleti
children.description: Oustalet's red colobus (Piliocolobus oustaleti) is a species of red colobus monkey..

children.name: Piliocolobus preussi
children.description: Preuss's red colobus (Piliocolobus preussi) is a red colobus primate species endemic to the Cross-Sanaga Rivers ecoregion..

children.name: Piliocolobus langi
children.description: Lang's red colobus (Piliocolobus langi) is a species of red colobus monkey..

children.name: Procolobus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the olive colobus, the smallest colobine monkey and one of the most cryptic primates of the West African rainforest. The olive colobus is the only colobine to carry its young in its mouth rather than clinging to the ventrum.

children.name: Procolobus verus
children.description: The olive colobus monkey (Procolobus verus), also known as the green colobus or Van Beneden's colobus, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

children.name: Semnopithecus
children.description: The grey langurs or Hanuman langurs are among the most widespread leaf monkeys of South Asia, venerated in Hinduism as representatives of the god Hanuman. They are highly tolerant of human presence and can be found in cities, temples, and farmland as well as forests.

children.name: Semnopithecus entellus
children.description: The northern plains gray langur (Semnopithecus entellus), also known as the sacred langur, Bengal sacred langur and Hanuman langur, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Semnopithecus schistaceus
children.description: The Nepal gray langur (Semnopithecus schistaceus) is a gray langur endemic to the Himalayas in Nepal, far southwestern Tibet, northern India, northern Pakistan, Bhutan and possibly Afghanistan..

children.name: Semnopithecus priam
children.description: The tufted gray langur (Semnopithecus priam), also known as Madras gray langur, and Coromandel sacred langur, is an Old World monkey, one of the species of langurs..

children.name: Semnopithecus dussumieri
children.description: Southern plains gray langur was the common name ascribed to Semnopithecus dussumieri by Mammal Species of the World (3rd edition) in 2005..

children.name: Semnopithecus hector
children.description: The Tarai gray langur (Semnopithecus hector) is an Old World monkey, and was formerly considered a subspecies of the northern plains gray langur..

children.name: Semnopithecus hypoleucos
children.description: The black-footed gray langur (Semnopithecus hypoleucos) is an Old World monkey, one of the species of langurs..

children.name: Semnopithecus ajax
children.description: The Kashmir gray langur (Semnopithecus ajax) is an Old World monkey, one of the langur species..

children.name: Trachypithecus
children.description: Lutungs, or banded leaf monkeys — a diverse group of colobine monkeys distributed across South and Southeast Asia. Many species are born bright orange and gradually darken to their adult colouration, creating striking nursery groups within troops.

children.name: Trachypithecus cristatus
children.description: The silvery lutung (Trachypithecus cristatus), also known as the silvered leaf monkey or the silvery langur, is an Old World monkey.

children.name: Trachypithecus phayrei
children.description: Phayre's leaf monkey (Trachypithecus phayrei), also known as Phayre's langur, is a species of Old World monkey native to South Asia and Southeast Asia, namely India, Bangladesh, and Myanmar..

children.name: Trachypithecus obscurus
children.description: The dusky leaf monkey (Trachypithecus obscurus), also known as the spectacled langur or the spectacled leaf monkey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Trachypithecus auratus
children.description: The East Javan langur (Trachypithecus auratus), also known as the ebony lutung, Javan langur or Javan lutung, is an Old World monkey from the Colobinae subfamily..

children.name: Trachypithecus francoisi
children.description: François' langur (Trachypithecus francoisi), also known as Francois' leaf monkey, the Tonkin leaf monkey, or the white side-burned black langur is a species of Old World monkey and the type species of its species group..

children.name: Trachypithecus delacouri
children.description: Delacour's langur or Delacour's lutung (Trachypithecus delacouri) is a critically endangered species of Old World monkey endemic to northern Vietnam..

children.name: Trachypithecus poliocephalus

children.name: Rhinopithecus
children.description: Snub-nosed monkeys are specialised high-altitude colobines of China and adjacent Southeast Asia, bearing upturned nostrils without an external nasal bone. children.name: Rhinopithecus roxellana

children.name: Simias

children.name: Nasalis

children.name: Nasalis larvatus
